title: SECTION 1, UNIT 3
subtitle: Distinguish subtle suffix variations in cephalosporins, psychotropics, and critical care sedatives (ceFAZolin/cefTRIAXone, fentaNYL/SUFentanil).

lasaPairs.feature: Spectrum-of-activity mismatch leading to therapeutic failure in serious CNS or multi-drug resistant bacterial infections.
Dosing interval mismatches, potential bleeding risk/coagulopathy associated with the N-methylthiotetrazole (NMTT) chain in cefotetan.
Inadequate coverage for Pseudomonas aeruginosa infections, leading to sepsis and therapeutic failure.
Profound, protracted hypoglycemia in non-diabetic patients vs. extreme sedation, dystonia, and neuroleptic side effects.
Unintended ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (OHSS) vs. cardiotoxicity, anticholinergic toxicity, and seizure risk.
Acute organ transplant rejection / nephrotoxicity from cyclosporine errors, or neurotoxicity and failed TB management from cycloserine errors.
Extreme bone marrow suppression, tissue necrosis, and severe toxicity from accidentally administering chemotherapy for an infection.
Dosing discrepancy (dimenhydrinate contains roughly half the milligram potency of diphenhydramine), leading to under- or over-sedation.
Depo-Medrol injected intravenously can cause fatal microembolism, respiratory arrest, and cardiac arrest; it is strictly contraindicated for IV use.
Sufentanil is roughly 5 to 10 times more potent than fentanyl; confusing doses causes immediate, lethal respiratory depression.
Pharmacologically opposing mechanisms: risperidone blocks dopamine (worsening Parkinson's), while ropinirole can trigger psychosis.
Crystalluria, acute renal injury, allergic hypersensitivity reactions, or untreated parasitic infections.
Different milligram potencies and pharmacokinetics triggering severe, unpredictable hypoglycemia.
